mainTopic: Who may testify that a בכור's blemish was not made on purpose: shepherds, outsiders, owners and household members
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining one reading of the משנה about who is believed to say that a בכור's blemish happened by itself. In that reading, a כהן working for a ישראל is believed. A ישראל working for a כהן is not believed, and a כהן testifying for another כהן is certainly not believed. It then asks why רבי מאיר is listed separately, and answers with the ברייתא of רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי, which requires two outsiders. In the same ברייתא, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows the כהן's son or daughter to testify, and רבי יוסי does not trust household members. רב קטינא requires two outsiders for a ספק בכור in a ישראל's house. רב נחמן proves that the ישראל owners themselves may testify, because only כהנים are suspected of making blemishes. The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a son and daughter may testify, but not a wife. Finally רב פפא asks how כהנים can judge at all according to רבי מאיר. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Why a priest-shepherd working for an Israelite is believed
steps.stepSummary: The כהן shepherd has no reason to lie, because he assumes the ישראל owner will give the בכור to a learned כהן and not to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thinks to himself: My boss will not skip over a Torah scholar and give the animal to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation of why a כהן who works as a shepherd for a ישראל is believed when he says a בכור's blemish happened by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished בכור goes to a כהן, so we might fear the shepherd is lying to get it. But the shepherd knows the owner will likely give it to a תלמיד חכם who is a כהן, not to a simple shepherd. So he gains nothing by lying, and his word is trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal, which is given to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: The person speaking here is the כהן shepherd, not the owner. He is the one who expects that the בכור will go to someone else.

phrases.english: He says to himself:
phrases.notes: This is the כהן working as a shepherd for a ישראל owner.

phrases.english: He will not pass over a Torah scholar
and give it to me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an explanation of the משנה that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן shepherd of a ישראל is believed, since he does not expect to receive the בכור.

steps.title: Israelite shepherds working for a priest are not believed
steps.stepSummary: A ישראל shepherd of a כהן is not believed, because the כהן might reward him with a taste of the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Shepherds of priests' means the shepherds are Israelites. They are not believed, because we worry they will lie for a bite of the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next case of the משנה in this reading: a ישראל who works for a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the owner is the כהן, so he would keep the blemished בכור and eat it. The ישראל shepherd might lie to please him, hoping to be given a mouthful. That small gain is enough to make his testimony untrustworthy.

keyTerms.meaning: Shepherds of priests, meaning shepherds who work for a כהן
A swallow or bite of food, a small reward

phrases.english: 'Shepherds of priests,' and they are Israelites:
they are not believed,
because we are concerned about a bite of food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the believed case to the case that is not believed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ישראל shepherd of a כהן is not believed, out of concern for לגימא.

steps.title: A priest testifying for another priest is certainly not believed
steps.stepSummary: A כהן testifying for another כהן has two reasons to be suspected: they may do favors for each other, and he may want a bite.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the more so a priest for another priest, because we worry about returning favors, and we also worry about a bite of the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a stronger case. If a ישראל working for a כהן is not believed, a כהן testifying for a כהן is surely not believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case has the same worry about a bite of food. On top of that, two כהנים might help each other: I testify for your בכור today, you testify for mine tomorrow. With two reasons for suspicion, this is a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Paying each other back, trading favors

phrases.english: And all the more so a priest for a priest,
because we are concerned about returning favors,
and we are concerned about a bite of food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a stronger case on top of step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן is not believed for another כהן, because of both גומלין and לגימא.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: believed for another, not for himself
steps.stepSummary: In this reading, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל comes to say that a כהן is believed about a friend's בכור but not about his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבן שמעון comes to say: he is believed about his friend's animal, but not about his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds in the משנה according to this reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא worried about a כהן testifying for another כהן. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees and does not suspect trading favors, so a כהן is believed for a friend. He is not believed only about his own animal, where he clearly benefits.

phrases.english: And רבן שמעון comes to say:
he is believed about his friend's animal,
but he is not believed about his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רבן שמעון בן גמליאל differs from the case in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן is believed about another's בכור but not about his own.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: a suspected person may not judge or testify
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר comes to say that anyone suspected about a matter may not judge it or testify about it, even for someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר comes to say: one who is suspected about a matter may not judge it and may not testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes this reading of the משנה by explaining what רבי מאיר adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is the opposite of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Since a כהן is suspected of making a מום in his own בכור, he cannot be trusted about this matter at all, even when it is someone else's animal.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is suspected about this matter
And he may not testify about it

steps.whatToRemember: In this reading there are three levels: the תנא קמא distrusts a כהן for another כהן, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל trusts him for another, and רבי מאיר never trusts a suspected person on this matter.

phrases.english: And רבי מאיר comes to say:
one who is suspected about a matter
may not judge it and may not testify about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the last opinion of the משנה to complete this reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person suspected about a matter may neither judge it nor testify about it.

steps.title: Under one reading, רבי מאיר adds something new
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that if the תנא קמא trusts a כהן working for a ישראל, then רבי מאיר is adding a real disagreement.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says that Israelite-owned shepherds who are priests are believed. That is why רבי מאיר comes to say: one who is suspected about a matter may not judge it or testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a difficulty. First it shows the reading where רבי מאיר's statement makes good sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנא קמא says a כהן shepherd of a ישראל is believed, then רבי מאיר is disagreeing: a כהן is suspected about בכור blemishes, so he is not believed even here. This prepares the contrast in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: It works well according to the one who says:
Shepherds of Israelites who are priests are believed;
that is why רבי מאיר comes to say:

phrases.aramaic: הֶחָשׁוּד עַל הַדָּבָר לֹא דָּנוֹ וְלֹא מְעִידוֹ.
phrases.english: one who is suspected about a matter may not judge it and may not testify about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from explaining the משנה to testing the two readings against רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ways of reading the תנא קמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the first half of the challenge: under this reading, רבי מאיר clearly disagrees with the תנא קמא.

steps.title: Under the other reading, רבי מאיר seems to add nothing
steps.stepSummary: If the תנא קמא already says priest shepherds in a ישראל's house are not believed, רבי מאיר is just repeating the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says that priest shepherds in an Israelite's house are not believed, what is רבי מאיר coming to teach us? That is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא makes the challenge. Under the other reading, רבי מאיר's statement seems to say nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנא קמא already distrusts a כהן working for a ישראל, he already treats the כהן as suspected even when it is not his own animal. That is exactly רבי מאיר's rule, so why does the משנה list רבי מאיר as a separate opinion?

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Both readings agree on the words of the משנה. They argue only about whether the תנא קמא trusts a כהן working for a ישראל, and that is what decides whether רבי מאיר adds anything.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says:

phrases.aramaic: רוֹעֵי כֹהֲנִים בֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין נֶאֱמָנִין —
phrases.english: Priest shepherds in an Israelite's house are not believed;
what is רבי מאיר coming to teach us?
That is the same as the תנא קמא!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא/אלא contrast begun in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the תנא קמא does not trust a כהן shepherd of a ישראל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, רבי מאיר's rule is the same as the תנא קמא, so his separate statement in the משנה would be pointless.

steps.title: The real difference: the view of רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא and רבי מאיר disagree about whether any two outsiders, even כהנים, may testify about a כהן's בכור. The תנא קמא holds like רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי, who allows this.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a practical difference between them: the view of רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי says, a בכור in a כהן's house needs two people from the marketplace to testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 7. רבי מאיר is not just repeating the תנא קמא, because the two disagree about something real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי only requires that the two witnesses come 'from the marketplace', meaning people outside the owner's household. Even a כהן qualifies, as long as he is independent. The תנא קמא agrees with this and only disqualifies a כהן who works as the shepherd. רבי מאיר disqualifies any כהן, because a person suspected about a matter cannot testify about it.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a practical difference between them
A firstborn animal, which belongs to the כהן
From the marketplace, meaning outsiders who are not part of the owner's household

steps.confusionAlert: 'From the marketplace' does not mean the witnesses must be ישראלים. It only means they are not members of the owner's household. They can be כהנים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the מתניתין from the problem raised in step 7. Each opinion now has its own clear position.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
regarding the view of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קַפּוֹסַאי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai says:
A firstborn animal in the house of a priest
requires two people from the marketplace
to testify about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קַפּוֹסַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7's challenge that רבי מאיר would just be repeating the תנא קמא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a practical difference between the two opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the תנא קמא disqualifies priest shepherds, it seemed רבי מאיר adds nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא accepts an independent כהן, like רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי. רבי מאיר rejects any כהן.

steps.title: The rest of the ברייתא: son, daughter, and household members
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows even the כהן's son or daughter to testify. רבי יוסי says even ten household members may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: even his son, even his daughter may testify. רבי יוסי says: even if there are ten of them, if they are members of his household, they may not testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא of רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי. Two more תנאים give their views on household members.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא has his own view. רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי requires two outsiders. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל trusts even the owner's own children. רבי יוסי says household members do not count, no matter how many there are, though רש״י explains that for him a single outsider is enough.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Even his son, even his daughter.
Rabbi Yosei says:
Even ten, if they are members of his household,
may not testify about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ בְּנוֹ, אֲפִילּוּ בִּתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא brought in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל trusts even the owner's children. רבי יוסי disqualifies any number of household members.

steps.title: Whose view is רב קטינא's rule about a doubtful בכור?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא supports רב קטינא's rule. That rule says a ספק בכור born in a ישראל's house needs two outsiders to testify about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this statement follow? רב חסדא said in the name of רב קטינא: a doubtful בכור born in a ישראל's house needs two people from the marketplace to testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related rule from an אמורא and asks which תנא it matches. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ספק בכור stays with the ישראל, and he may eat it once it has a blemish. That gives him a reason to blemish it on purpose, just like a כהן with a בכור. So the rule requires two outside witnesses, and the גמרא wants to find which תנא is the source for this requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose status as a firstborn is uncertain
In the house, meaning the possession, of a ישראל

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is this

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב קַטִּינָא:
phrases.english: that Rav Ḥisda said that Rav Ketina said:
A doubtful firstborn that was born in the house of an Israelite,

phrases.aramaic: צָרִיךְ שְׁנַיִם מִן הַשּׁוּק לְהָעִיד עָלָיו?
phrases.english: requires two people from the marketplace to testify about it?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב קַטִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא just quoted to locate the source of a later אמורא's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's opinion supports requiring two outside witnesses for a ספק בכור in a ישראל's house.

steps.title: It follows רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא's rule follows רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי, who requires two outsiders for a בכור held by someone who might want to blemish it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view? It follows רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. רב קטינא's rule matches the view of רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי requires two outsiders for a כהן's בכור, because the כהן is suspected of making the blemish himself. A ישראל holding a ספק בכור is suspected in the same way. So the same rule of two outsiders applies to him.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with, following the view of

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of 'two from the marketplace' comes from רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי. It is the basis for the תנא קמא trusting an independent כהן, and for רב קטינא requiring outside witnesses for a ספק בכור in a ישראל's house.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
In accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב קטינא's rule follows רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי, who requires two outside witnesses whenever the owner is suspected of making the blemish.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the owners themselves may testify
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the ישראל owners may testify about their own animal's blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The owners may testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a different view from רב קטינא. He says the ישראל owners themselves may testify about their ספק בכור's blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב קטינא needed two outsiders, because the owner might want the animal blemished. רב נחמן says the owner himself is trusted, so no outside witnesses are needed. His proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the owners (here, the ישראל who owns the animal)

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
The owners may testify about it,
phrases.notes: He means the ישראל owners of the ספק בכור from רב קטינא's case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a view that argues on רב קטינא's rule from Steps 10-11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ישראל owners are believed to testify about the blemish on their own ספק בכור.

steps.title: First proof: who could testify about מעשר according to רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן argues that if owners could not testify, nobody could testify about a blemished מעשר animal according to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if you do not say so, then for מעשר, according to רבי מאיר, who could testify about it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a proof for his rule. He points to a מעשר animal, which also may not be eaten as ordinary meat until it has a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that someone suspected on a matter cannot testify about it. If every owner were suspected of making blemishes, nobody could ever testify about a blemished מעשר animal. So owners must be trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: the animal tithe: every tenth animal of the flock, which is holy
because if you do not say so (introduces a proof)

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
then for the animal tithe, according to Rabbi Meir,
who can testify about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן's rule from Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's rule that the owners may testify.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of a blemished מעשר animal according to רבי מאיר: someone must be able to testify about it.

steps.title: מעשר is different: the owner could blemish his whole flock
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: the owner of מעשר is trusted for a special reason that does not apply to בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: With מעשר, the owner is certainly believed, because if he wanted, he could put a blemish on his entire flock.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from מעשר. The owner of a מעשר animal has a special reason to be trusted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the tithe is separated, the owner may legally blemish his whole flock. So he has no reason to secretly blemish one מעשר animal, and he is believed. This does not show that owners are trusted in general, so it proves nothing about a בכור.

phrases.english: With the tithe, he is certainly believed,
because if he wanted, he could put a blemish
phrases.notes: He could do this legally, before the duty to separate the tithe takes effect.

phrases.english: on his entire flock.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from מעשר in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from מעשר is rejected. רב נחמן's rule itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The owner of מעשר is trusted only because he could legally blemish his whole flock. That reason does not apply to a בכור.

steps.title: Better proof: who could testify about a ספק בכור?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן's proof is restated using ספק בכור: according to רבי מאיר, nobody else could testify about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, for a ספק בכור, according to רבי מאיר, who could testify about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes רב נחמן's proof so that it uses a ספק בכור instead of מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a ספק בכור, both a ישראל and a כהן gain if it gets a blemish. If the ישראל owner is not trusted, and כהנים are suspected too, then according to רבי מאיר nobody could testify. That would leave the animal with no way to be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: an animal that may or may not be a firstborn
rather (introduces a corrected version of the argument)

phrases.english: Rather, for an animal that may be a firstborn,
according to Rabbi Meir, who can testify about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof from מעשר with a proof from ספק בכור.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's rule that the owners may testify.
steps.raayaSupportSource: If owners were not trusted, nobody could testify about a ספק בכור according to רבי מאיר.

steps.title: A משנה shows רבי מאיר allows a ספק בכור to be eaten
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say a ספק בכור simply has no fix. The גמרא answers that a משנה shows רבי מאיר discusses eating such an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that it really has no fix, did we not learn: רבי יוסי used to say, any animal whose replacement is in a כהן's hand is exempt from the gifts, and רבי מאיר obligates?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible escape from the proof. It brings a משנה to show that רבי מאיר does allow a ספק בכור to be slaughtered and eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could answer that according to רבי מאיר, a ספק בכור can never be eaten. But in the משנה, רבי מאיר requires the priestly gifts from such an animal, which means it is slaughtered and eaten. So someone must be able to testify about its blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: the priestly gifts (foreleg, cheeks and stomach) given from a slaughtered animal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this משנה is about the testimony itself. It is brought only to show that, according to רבי מאיר, a ספק בכור can be eaten. That means someone must be able to testify about its blemish.

phrases.english: And if you would say that indeed
it has no remedy,
phrases.notes: He means the ספק בכור could never be made fit to eat, since no one could testify about its blemish.

phrases.english: but didn't we learn that Rabbi Yosei would say:
Any animal whose replacement is in the hand of a priest
phrases.notes: This is the ספק בכור: the other animal of the doubt was given to the כהן, so the כהן already holds what may be the real בכור (רש״י).

phrases.english: is exempt from the priestly gifts,
and Rabbi Meir obligates!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלֵית לֵיהּ תַּקַּנְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the proof in Step 15 by ruling out the answer that a ספק בכור simply has no fix.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי מאיר, a ספק בכור can be eaten, so someone must be able to testify about it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (18b) where רבי מאיר requires the priestly gifts from an animal whose replacement is in a כהן's hand.

steps.title: Only כהנים are suspected of making blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ישראל owners may testify, because only כהנים are suspected of blemishing animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: the owners may testify about it. It is כהנים who are suspected about blemishes; ישראלים are not suspected about blemishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב נחמן's proof and states his conclusion. A ישראל owner is believed about his ספק בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי מאיר lets a ספק בכור be eaten, someone must be trusted to testify about it. That person is the ישראל owner, because only כהנים are suspected of making blemishes. This argues with רב קטינא, who required two outsiders.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, a ישראל owner may testify about his own ספק בכור's blemish. Only כהנים are suspected of making blemishes, and a ישראל is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: For רב נחמן, the rule of 'two outsiders' is aimed only at כהנים. Unlike רב קטינא in step 10, he holds that a ישראל was never under that suspicion.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
The owners may testify about it,
it is priests who are suspected about blemishes,
Israelites are not suspected about blemishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof in Steps 15-16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ישראל owners may testify about their ספק בכור, because only כהנים are suspected of making blemishes.

steps.title: רב נחמן and רבא disagree about the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and רבא rules like רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: רב נחמן says the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רבא says the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two אמוראים who disagree about which earlier opinion is the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל trusts a כהן's household members to testify about his בכור's blemish. רבי יוסי does not trust them. So רב נחמן trusts the household, and רבא does not.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Nachman says:
The halacha is like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
Rava says: The halacha is like Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא of step 9 and brings an אמוראי dispute over whether the halacha follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל or רבי יוסי about a כהן's household members.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: household members are trusted (like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל). רבא: they are not trusted (like רבי יוסי).

steps.title: רבא seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: Another statement of רבא seems to trust the household members to testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבא really say this? But רבא said: if the owners were standing outside with us, and the animal went in whole and came out hurt, they may testify about it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא from another statement of his that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that statement, the animal was hurt inside the house while the owners were outside, and someone testifies that no person caused the blemish. That sounds like the household is trusted, which goes against רבא's ruling like רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? (opens a contradiction)
Owners (here, the כהן and his family)

phrases.english: And did Rava say this?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רָבָא: בְּעָלִים עוֹמְדִים עִמָּנוּ בַּחוּץ,
phrases.english: But Rava said: If the owners were standing outside with us,

phrases.aramaic: נִכְנַס שָׁלֵם וְיָצָא חָבוּל — מְעִידִין עָלָיו!
phrases.english: and it went in whole and came out injured, they testify about it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רָבָא הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's ruling from step 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא himself says the household may testify about the blemish, which goes against רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The whole family was outside
steps.stepSummary: רבא's statement means all the family members were outside, and we do not suspect the one who testifies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it like this: all the owners were standing outside, and we are not worried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by reading רבא's statement in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Owners" means the entire household was outside, so the one who testifies is not a family member. We trust that outsider and do not worry he caused the blemish. So רבא never said family members may testify.

keyTerms.meaning: All the owners, the whole household
We are not worried, we do not suspect

phrases.english: Say: all the owners were standing outside,
and we are not concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's statement seemed to trust the family members.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole family was outside, and the trusted witness is not one of them.

steps.title: Then why say it at all?
steps.stepSummary: If the family was outside, it seems obvious that the outsider is trusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is he teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say something that now seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once no family member is involved, it seems clear that the witness should be trusted. So the new reading looks like it makes רבא's statement unnecessary.

phrases.english: If so, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that all the owners were outside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no family member is involved, רבא's ruling seems too obvious to need saying.

steps.title: We might have suspected the witness himself
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that we do not suspect the person inside of causing the blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said we should worry about suspicion. He teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what new point רבא's statement teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person who stayed inside with the animal could be suspected of hurting it himself. רבא teaches that we do not worry about this, and he is trusted.

phrases.english: You might have said: let us be concerned about suspicion,
he teaches us that we are not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 by showing רבא's statement teaches something new.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might suspect the person inside of causing the blemish.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not suspect him, so he may testify.

steps.title: Final ruling: son and daughter yes, wife no
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but only a son or daughter may testify, not a wife, because a wife counts like the man himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but only his son and daughter, not his wife. Why? His wife is like himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final הלכה and sets a limit on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Family members may testify about a כהן's בכור, like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. But a wife is treated as one person with her husband. Since the כהן cannot testify about his own בכור, his wife cannot either.

keyTerms.meaning: His wife is like his own self

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן's son or daughter may testify that his בכור's blemish was not made by a person, but his wife may not, because she counts like him.
steps.confusionAlert: This ruling follows רב נחמן's view, not רבא's, even though the גמרא just defended רבא from a contradiction. Answering a question on רבא does not mean the הלכה follows him.

phrases.english: And the halacha is like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
and only his son and his daughter,
but not his wife.
What is the reason? His wife is like his own body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the disagreement from step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הלכה like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a son and daughter may testify, but a wife may not, since she is like the כהן himself.

steps.title: How can priests judge according to רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי: if a suspected person cannot judge, and suspicion on one thing means suspicion on everything, כהנים could never judge. But a פסוק says they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: רבי מאיר says someone suspected about a matter may not judge it or testify about it. He also says someone suspected about one thing is suspected about the whole Torah. Does that mean כהנים may not judge at all? But it is written: "By their word shall every dispute and every נגע be decided"!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא puts two rules of רבי מאיר together and shows they seem to clash with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כהנים are suspected of blemishing בכורות. Under רבי מאיר, that suspicion should spread to the whole Torah, so a כהן could never judge any case. But the פסוק says כהנים do decide disputes and נגעים.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is suspected about a matter
He may not judge it or testify about it
A skin affliction that a כהן must judge

steps.whyThisMatters: It forces the גמרא to explain how far רבי מאיר's rule about a חשוד really goes.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
According to Rabbi Meir, who says

phrases.aramaic: הֶחָשׁוּד עַל הַדָּבָר לֹא דָּנוֹ וְלֹא מְעִידוֹ,
phrases.english: one who is suspected about a matter may neither judge it nor testify about it,
and Rabbi Meir also says

phrases.aramaic: הֶחָשׁוּד לְדָבָר אֶחָד חָשׁוּד לְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ,
phrases.english: one suspected about one matter is suspected about the entire Torah,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּהֲנִים הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלָא דָּיְינִי דִּינָא?
phrases.english: do priests also not judge any case?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכְתִיב ״וְעַל פִּיהֶם יִהְיֶה כׇּל רִיב וְכׇל נָגַע״!
phrases.english: But it is written: "And by their word shall every dispute and every affliction be"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about רבי מאיר's rule of a חשוד from the משנה (step 5). It combines that rule with his other rule that one suspected on one matter is suspected on the whole Torah.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's rules about a חשוד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Putting together "a suspected person may not judge" and "suspected on one thing means suspected on all" would bar all כהנים from judging, against the פסוק.
